Jump to: Contact us Reimagining higher education partnerships SOAS's Strategic Plan articulates a vision for a new model of international partnerships that is responsive to the transnational character of our global challenges. There is an urgent need for international partnerships which are more equitable in nature, requiring a fundamental rethinking of partnership models to enable the co-development, co-teaching and co-accreditation of academic programmes in a much more integrated way. Our vision Play video Visit SOAS If you and your delegation would like to visit us in London to discuss plans to collaborate or if you have any questions about our partnerships, please get in touch. Send us a message Partnership models Joint programmes Open Universities often talk about equitable partnerships but there is little understanding of what this truly means. This is because it is difficult to establish equitable partnerships in an unequal world. Instead, most partnerships concern student mobility, often taking the form of international exchanges or dual degrees – students begin their studies at one institution and move to another. But what is needed are joint programmes that bring knowledge systems into conversation with each other so that we can tackle the transnational challenges facing us today. With our new equitable partnerships, we aim to do just this. These unique programmes developed in partnership with institutions across Africa, Asia and the Middle East are co-designed, co-taught and co-accredited with a single fee charged to all students. Each programme explores a key global issue from a Global South-Global North perspective, providing students with a rich learning experience that crosses knowledge systems. Dual programmes Open SOAS is working with a growing number of university partners to offer students a range of dual degree programmes (at undergraduate and postgraduate level), as well as progression and articulation arrangements. Dual degrees provide students with the opportunity to take degrees at (and receive two separate awards from) two different universities in a shorter amount of time than it would take to complete both degrees separately. to: Contact us Guidance for international applicants Agent representatives support international students with their applicant journey on behalf of SOAS. This includes providing guidance on best-fit degree programmes, support with completing applications, and offering post-application guidance across topics such as student visas, accommodation, and funding. Each approved agent listed below is carefully selected by the SOAS International Office and holds a direct contract with the university. This ensures that they are equipped with regular training, resources, and comprehensive knowledge to accurately advise applicants and represent SOAS. Where an applicant enrols through an approved agent, a monetary commission fee will be paid directly to the representative in recognition of services provided. All applications to SOAS are assessed equally according to our standard entry requirements and criteria. It is not compulsory to apply through an approved agent representative. If you are considering working with an agent, we recommend you read the British Council's guide to choosing an education agent . UK Agent Quality Framework Open SOAS University of London is committed to the UK Agent Quality Framework and pledges to create and maintain the highest standards of agent management, ensuring the UK remains a leading study destination for international students. The UK Agent Quality Framework (AQF) is an initiative led by the UK government and sector partners to promote professional and ethical standards among educational advisors representing UK institutions. It sets out a shared set of expectations and best practice to ensure that prospective students receive accurate, reliable, and trustworthy advice throughout their education journey. Our collaboration with global representatives is guided by the Agent Quality Framework (AQF), and we regularly review and monitor their work to ensure continued alignment with these standards. This enables SOAS to provide international students with a high-quality experience from the moment they begin exploring their options to their arrival at SOAS and beyond. Complaints process Open We are committed to working with education agents and advisors who provide honest, transparent, and student-focused support. If you have concerns about the behaviour or practices of an agent representing SOAS, we encourage you to let us know. We take all complaints seriously and will investigate any concerns raised about misrepresentation, unethical conduct, or a failure to meet expected standards. How to submit a complaint If you have a concern about an education agent representing SOAS, please complete the online complaints form with as much detail as possible. SOAS will acknowledge receipt of the complaint within five working days. All complaints will be handled confidentially and in accordance with our Educational Advisor and Agent Complaints Policy . Guide to choosing and education agent Open If you are considering working with an agent, we recommend you read the British Council's student and parent guide to choosing an education agent . Each approved agent listed below is carefully selected by the SOAS International Office and holds a direct contract with the university. This ensures that they are equipped with regular training, resources, and comprehensive knowledge to accurately advise applicants and represent SOAS. Where an applicant enrols through an approved agent, a monetary commission fee will be paid directly to the representative in recognition of services provided. All applications to SOAS are assessed equally according to our standard entry requirements and criteria. It is not compulsory to apply through an approved agent representative. Our collaboration with global representatives is guided by the Agent Quality Framework (AQF), and we regularly review and monitor their work to ensure continued alignment with these standards. takes place on the main SOAS campus in central London, giving students the opportunity to experience campus life in Bloomsbury while making the most of everything that a major capital city like London has to offer. If you want to study English in an academic setting or have the opportunity to follow an academic subject course using English, we offer a range of English language and introductory academic courses which can be studied over a 3, 6 or 9-week period between July and September. The academic courses cover arts and humanities as well as social science subjects, ranging from art and literature to international relations and development studies. The teaching style is highly interactive and uses London as an extension to the classroom. It provides a great introduction to studying at an English-speaking university. Application form Apply for the SOAS International Summer Programme. You must be at least 18 years of age to apply. Apply for the programme Teaching All courses consist of 18-20 hours of lesson time each week at SOAS University of London's Russell Square campus*. The English language courses cover development of all four language skills with a focus on reading and writing in the mornings and listening and speaking in the afternoons. The academic subject courses include lectures, seminar discussions and case studies, and support classes from a subject specialist English teacher. Students also carry out their own independent research and present their work at the end of the course. Students on the International Summer Programme have access to campus facilities including the university's world-famous library, and accommodation is available in nearby halls of residence. Students also use London as a context for further exploration by going on study trips to interesting and relevant places in this historic capital city. here: Home International Global Partnerships SOAS–Sophia University Graduate Dual Degree Programme The Department of Japan and Korea at SOAS, in collaboration with Sophia University's Graduate Programme in Global Studies (GPGS) is delighted to offer a Graduate Dual Degree Programme. The Dual MA is based at Sophia University, as Japanese Master’s programmes are typically 2-years long, and SOAS contributes to it by offering its MA in Japanese Studies as an option for students originally enrolled at Sophia University. For SOAS students there is the opportunity to continue studying in Japan for a further year after first completing the MA in Japanese Studies at SOAS. Students proceeding to Sophia University can add any one degree within the GPGS at Sophia University, while students coming from Sophia must choose the MA Japanese Studies from SOAS. Students will study 1-year at GPGS and 1-year at SOAS. Only upon successful completion of both the MA Japanese Studies at SOAS and the corresponding 1-year element at Sophia will students receive two MA degrees, one from each institution. For students considering enrolment through SOAS Applications are made to the 1-year MA Japanese Studies programme at SOAS. The continuation at Sophia is an optional add-on that has no impact on how the MA Japanese Studies is taught at SOAS and its normal rules and regulations apply. For students considering enrolment through SOAS, this is an opportunity to add one year of study at Sophia University, after they have completed the taught elements of their MA in Japanese Studies with SOAS. However, students should indicate interest in the possibility to continue to Sophia University upon the point of application. Only upon being accepted by Sophia University in a separate application procedure (please see below), can the students proceed to Japan. The fees for the MAs are to be paid separately to each institution. Application procedure Prospective students should apply in the first instance for the MA programme at the institution where they intend to commence their studies. If you want to study English in an academic setting or have the opportunity to follow an academic subject course using English, we offer a range of English language and introductory academic courses which can be studied over a 3, 6 or 9-week period between July and September. Contact Knowledge Transfer Partnerships at SOAS The Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) scheme helps businesses in the UK to innovate and grow. It does this by linking them with a university and a graduate. The scheme is part funded by a government grant. A KTP enables a business to bring in new skills and the latest academic thinking from SOAS to deliver a specific, strategic innovation project through a knowledge-based partnership. We can help you: develop your business and improve your business performance access academic expertise that you don’t have in-house help you to become more competitive and productive If you partner with SOAS, we will help to recruit a suitable graduate, known as an Associate. We will employ the Associate, but they will be based at your premises, working with you in the same way as any other member of your team. KTPs are strategic projects – the purpose of the partnership is to embed knowledge and expertise to make a real difference to how the company works in the future. The scheme can last between 12 and 36 months, depending on what the project is and the needs of your business. At SOAS, we have staff dedicated to working with you to make connections within SOAS, scope out the project, put together your application, and ensure that your KTP runs smoothly once awarded. If you are interested in partnering with SOAS on a KTP, please get in contact with the Enterprise team. Further services Consultancy The Enterprise Office helps to match clients’ needs to the most appropriate expertise within SOAS. Expert briefings We provide tailored briefings for global charities, senior diplomats or staff members being posted to Asia, Africa and the Middle East. Student Enterprise Students at SOAS have access to multiple mentoring programs, workshops and funding opportunities to hone their entrepreneurial skills. Jump to: Schemes Jump to: SOAS UKRI Fellows Jump to: SOAS research and knowledge exchange projects Jump to: More info Jump to: Contact us About We are excited to be supporting prospective researchers who wish to apply to be hosted at SOAS. Our research is globally recognised, with over half our disciplines landing in the top ten for universities following the Research Excellence Framework 2021 (REF), and 87% of the research that we submitted ranking ‘world leading’ or ‘internationally excellent’. Our Research and Knowledge Exchange strategy 2021-2026 (PDF, 564KB) outlines are plans for re-centring research excellence and intensivity. Support The structure and shape of the support will depend on the grant or fellowship you are awarded, but most will include a generous training and career development budget to enrich your skills as a researcher, and to build your network, profile and publication record. SOAS is a signatory to the HR Concordat for Excellence in Research, providing academic colleagues with a strong support network and framework for research development, as well as an Early Career Research forum to support researchers across the institution. All researchers who come to SOAS on the types of grants listed above will enjoy the status and benefits of that come with being a member of our academic community. They will have access to the facilities they need to carry out their work including access to the SOAS Library, one of the world's most important academic libraries for the study of Asia, Africa and the Middle East. You will have access to biddable funds for to develop their research and impact; mentoring and support via our Personal Research Plan process, and dedicated time to pursue specific career development activities. Schemes now taking applications UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship - Round 11 Open UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship - Round 11 SOAS is excited to support emerging and exceptional talent in various exciting research areas. The UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship Round 11 will open 2 February 2026, with the UKRI deadline 16 June 2026. It offers long-term, flexible support, including the fellow's salary and research, staff and training costs, plus the opportunity of a permanent academic position on successful completion of the fellowship. Due to the extremely competitive nature of these fellowships and a cap on the number of full stage applications that can be submitted per institution, SOAS is running a call for Expressions of Interest from both internal and external staff. Home Research Research And Knowledge Exchange The SOAS Research Ethics Policy sets out the ethical principles which staff, students and other researchers are expected to follow when conducting research under the auspices of SOAS. The policy, which has been approved by the Research & Knowledge Exchange Committee, defines the unacceptable behaviour which will be treated by the School as research misconduct. The policy can be found on the Policies and Procedures page . Policy for the investigation of allegations of research misconduct The SOAS policy for Investigating Allegations of Research Misconduct has been adopted from the model Procedure for the Investigation of Misconduct in Research published by the UK Research Integrity Office. It sets out how SOAS will undertake investigations that relate to allegations of research misconduct, as defined in the Research Ethics policy. All complaints relating to allegations of research misconduct must be submitted in writing and marked for the attention of the Schools' Registrar. The policy can be found on the Policies and Procedures page . Statement on Research Integrity SOAS continues in its commitment of striving to ensure research conducted under its auspices conforms to the revised Concordat to Support Research Integrity (October 2019). Home Research Research And Knowledge Exchange Our dedicated Research and Knowledge Exchange team facilitates the development of proposals and tenders, manages project budgets, advises on ethics, risk and due diligence, and supports impact and evaluation. We have a diverse portfolio of externally funded research, including grants awarded by: Arts and Humanities Research Council Economic and Social Research Council The British Academy The Leverhulme Trust Wellcome European Research Council European Commission Contact If you are interested in applying for research funding, please contact your Research and Knowledge Exchange Development Officer. Details of which Officers cover which Departments and Schools can be found on MySOAS . For general queries, please contact us on research@soas.ac.uk . Prospective Fellows We support Fellows from across the globe to come to SOAS to undertake high-standard research and develop their academic portfolios. We have hosted fellowships funded via organisations and schemes including the British Academy, the Leverhulme Trust, the Arts and Humanities Research Council, the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions, the UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship programme, and a range of specialist sponsors. If you would like to find out more about current opportunities at SOAS, please email research@soas.ac.uk . ESRC Impact Acceleration Account at SOAS SOAS has successfully secured an ESRC Impact Acceleration Account (IAA) for 2023-2028. Co-managed by the SOAS Centre for Migration and Diaspora Studies and the Research and Knowledge Exchange Directorate, the 5-year £1.25 million IAA boosts the impact of SOAS’ migration and marginalisation research. This thematically focused IAA will articulate with all aspects of SOAS’ strategies, mobilising nationally and globally urgent ground-breaking SOAS social science research on the precursors and effects of migration and displacement and of the construction of minorities and minority identities, and strengthening SOAS’ emergent and powerful decolonising partnership practices with policy, NGO and corporate sectors that result in positive action. A range of support is offered for SOAS researchers at every stage of their careers thematic roundtables that foster knowledge exchange between SOAS researchers and practitioners and policy makers an annual mobility programme of short-term, high impact knowledge exchange fellowships rapid response and strategic grants of £2,500 to £10,000 that support co-production of knowledge and impact-oriented outputs SOAS researchers will also be gain expertise in knowledge exchange practices and approaches through partner-led capacity building, and will have the opportunity of showcasing their research and engage the public during the annual ESRC Festival of Social Science .
